chapter: New Orleans style and bass playing
title: Where he played with Don Ewell; Ory's last time blowing
summary: Ewell played in the Ory band at various venues; Garland repeats the 1972 New Orleans story of holding the beat for the weak Ory.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Where'd you play with Don Ewell?
Oh, he played with us at the Ory band.
Yeah, played with Ory the first -- in Frisco
Yah, played at the Beverly Caverns.
oh, I didn't know, that's very interest-ing.
I played, the last I played with that Don, 1972 --
I went up to the show up there, New Orleans, yeah, no, no, no, New Orleans.
And Ory was there, that's when Ory couldn't play, he had no business leaving Honolulu, he was really sick. He got up there he couldn't play --

Seems like somebody in the audience ask, 'where's my Marduti Tootie,' and the man said, Oh, that is right. And they called Tootie, send him out here, and I crept across the stage there, and got up there and Ory was so weak, you understand, and he was so glad when I come, you know, because I know just what he wants to do, you know?
And, I pick up -- Ory always picks up his own numbers -- and he picked it up and picked up and -- but I held a strong beat there for him, you know. Helped him out.
So he could make it. That's the last time he blowed.
Oh. Yeah, then he went back, back to the --
